scope: easy_profiler.py and ecc_speedtest.py read whole. Standard Python 3 syntax parsing only; no profiler or ECC speed benchmark executed.

easy_profiler.py.message: Missing parentheses in call to 'print'. Did you mean print(...)?

findings: easy_profiler contains Python 2 print syntax; standard Python 3 parser rejects the module before any profiling branch.

Profiler branches join argument list using spaces and pass a string; quoting/argument boundaries can be lost. Stack branch instead passes list. Arbitrary script path is fed to __import__ after extension removal, not loaded by file path.

ECC benchmark uses process CPU time around codec only, excluding data generation and corruption. It reports msg_nb*max_block_size while generated payload length is message_size, so rates concern nominal codeword bytes, not input payload throughput.
ECC decoder benchmark accepts codeword check but does not compare recovered message to original. It prints decode failure warnings and still returns zero without failure counts.
Erasure mode zeroes positions but does not pass enable_erasures or positions into decode; benchmark help claims positions are provided, contradicting call.
Subchunk encoding uses undefined xrange under Python 3; string argv path uses shlex without importing shlex. Static branch failures, not executed benchmark results.
Random data consists of hexadecimal ASCII without a fixed seed. No paired before/after controls, dispersion, backend identity capture or end-to-end file-I/O measurement.
